subject: general
question: Field hockey used to be restarted by ‘Roll-in’. When was Roll-in replaced by ‘Push-in’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1970**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If the ball went out of play over the side-line, the play was initially restarted by rolling the ball (by hand) back into the field at right angles to the sideline.
 
• **In the 1970s the roll-in was replaced by a push-in (with the stick) and in 1984 the push-in was replaced by a hit-in, making it similar to a free hit**.
 
• A push pass is used to move the ball speedily over shorter distances.
 
• Because it gives you the most control over the ball, it is the best pass to use in short distances and it gives you more accuracy.
 
• Your stick will stay in contact with the ball until it is released for the pass.
